prompts.audio.episode.detailed: Plan a podcast episode. Topic: [topic]. Format: [solo, conversation, interview]. Length: [minutes] minutes. Timed blocks: intro, 3–4 main segments, takeaway, sign-off. For each segment, the main question and an example or story. List separately any facts that need checking.
prompts.audio.episode.refine: Make a plan for a 3-episode series on this topic.
prompts.audio.episode.check: Does the plan make clear why a listener would stay to the end?
prompts.audio.guest.short: Write 10 questions for a guest — [who, by role] — on “[topic]”.
prompts.audio.guest.detailed: Guest: [who, by role]. Topic: [topic]. Write 12 questions: 2 warm-ups, 7 on the topic (open, “how”, “why”, “give an example”), 2 unexpected ones, 1 closing. No yes-or-no questions. Mark 3 spare questions in case the conversation moves faster.
prompts.audio.guest.refine: Add follow-ups for question [number] in case the guest answers too briefly.
prompts.audio.guest.check: Are any questions too personal or awkward? How could I rephrase them?
prompts.audio.intro.detailed: Write 3 intros for the episode “[topic]”, each 20–30 seconds read aloud: one opening with a question, one with a short story, one with what the listener will get. Include the podcast name [name], what the episode covers and why to stay. Write for the ear: short sentences, no complex structures.
prompts.audio.intro.refine: Make option [number] warmer and more conversational.
prompts.audio.intro.check: How many seconds will this intro take at a calm pace? [text]
prompts.audio.host.short: Write host notes for the episode: [outline]
prompts.audio.host.detailed: From the episode outline, write host notes: for each block, keywords, a fact or figure (marked “checked” or “to check”), the transition to the next block, a backup question. Mark spots for a pause and for addressing the listeners. Outline: [outline]
prompts.audio.host.refine: Add short bridging phrases in case I lose my train of thought.
prompts.audio.host.check: Which facts in the notes haven't I checked yet? Make a list.
prompts.audio.aloud.short: Rewrite this text so it's easy to read aloud: [text]
prompts.audio.aloud.detailed: Adapt the text for reading aloud or text-to-speech: split long sentences, replace brackets and footnotes with words, write numbers and abbreviations as they're spoken, remove things that only work visually (tables, “see above”). Don't change the meaning. Text: [text]
prompts.audio.aloud.refine: Mark words where text-to-speech might get the stress wrong and suggest a workaround.
prompts.audio.aloud.check: Compare my adaptation with the original: has the meaning changed? [adaptation]
prompts.audio.pauses.short: Mark where to pause in this text: [text]
prompts.audio.pauses.detailed: Mark up the text for reading: “/” for a short pause, “//” for a long one, and highlight words that need emphasis. Explain the 3 most important spots and why a pause matters there. Don't change the words. Text: [text]
prompts.audio.pauses.refine: Where can I speed up so it doesn't sound monotonous?
prompts.audio.pauses.check: I read the text in [seconds] seconds. Is that too fast for [audience]?
prompts.audio.title.short: Suggest 8 titles for an episode about [topic].
prompts.audio.title.detailed: The episode is about [topic], main idea: [idea]. Suggest 10 titles of different kinds: a question, a promise of value, a guest quote (only if I provide one: [quote]), a teaser, a plain description. Up to 60 characters. Mark which are easiest to find by search.
prompts.audio.title.refine: Make the titles consistent across the whole series.
prompts.audio.title.check: The title “[title]”: would a new listener know what the episode is about?
prompts.audio.description.short: Write an episode description from the outline: [outline]
prompts.audio.description.detailed: Write an episode description for podcast platforms: 2–3 sentences on what it covers and what the listener will learn, a topic list with timestamps (if I provide them: [timestamps]), mentioned materials, the guest by role. No exaggeration and no guest contact details. Outline: [outline]
prompts.audio.description.refine: Make a short version under 280 characters for social media.
prompts.audio.description.check: Does the description match what was actually said? [what was said]
prompts.audio.rights.short: What should I check about rights to music and voices for my podcast?
prompts.audio.rights.detailed: I want to use in the episode: [what I'm using: music, clips, voices, AI voice-over]. Make a checklist of rights questions for each: who the author is, which licence, whether commercial use is allowed, whether credit is required, whether the person consented to recording and to voice cloning. No legal conclusions, just questions.
prompts.audio.rights.refine: Where can I find music with a clear licence for a podcast? Name types of sources.
prompts.audio.rights.check: Help me write a credits line for the episode description: [what was used]
prompts.audio.cleanup.short: How can I clean up noise in this recording: [problem]?
prompts.audio.cleanup.detailed: Here are the recording's problems: [problem]. Software: [software]. Suggest an order of processing: noise reduction, levelling, removing clicks and breaths, EQ. For each step — why, what to watch for, how not to ruin the voice. If you're unsure about the software's features, say so.
prompts.audio.cleanup.refine: How can I record the next episode so there's less to clean up?
prompts.audio.cleanup.check: After processing the voice sounds [description]. What might I have overdone?

verify.audio.episode: Check the plan against real timing: read at least the intro aloud and time it.
verify.audio.guest: Before recording, ask your guest what they're happy to talk about and what not. Don't use personal information without consent.
verify.audio.intro: The intro should sound natural when you say it. Read it aloud and fix any words you trip over.
verify.audio.host: Notes are a crib sheet, not a script. A podcast read off the page sounds flat.
verify.audio.aloud: Synthetic voices can misplace stress in names and terms. Listen to the whole thing before publishing.
verify.audio.pauses: Pauses can only be checked by ear. Record a section and listen back.
verify.audio.title: The title should honestly reflect the episode. Don't promise what isn't in it.
verify.audio.description: List sources and mentioned materials in the description, after checking the links.
verify.audio.rights: This isn't legal advice. Read licence terms on the services' and authors' official pages.
verify.audio.cleanup: Keep the original recording: it's easy to overdo processing, and you can't undo it without the original.
